title: Evidence for cavity-induced metallic phase from entropic electron correlation effects
summary: Experiments have revealed that collective strong coupling in optical cavities can drastically alter the conductivity and dielectric properties of molecular ensembles, or even trigger abrupt phase transitions (in Rayleigh scattering or dispersion force driven conformational equilibrium). Until now, the underlying physical mechanism has remained unknown. A recently proposed theory attributes these collective effects to cavity-induced electron correlations that share properties of the known spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model of a spin glass.
